# Compute highest Natural_Cause

highest_natural_cause_juristiction = highest_row["Jurisdiction_of_Occurrence"]

# Compute highest Septicemia

```{python}
# Largest 20 countries by Life Expectancy (bar chart) with a blue color scale
# Group by 'Jurisdiction_of_Occurrence' and sum 'All_Cause' deaths
jurisdiction_deaths = wkds_2023.groupby('Jurisdiction_of_Occurrence')['All_Cause'].sum().reset_index()

# Sort by 'All_Cause' deaths in descending order
jurisdiction_deaths_sorted = jurisdiction_deaths.sort_values(by='All_Cause', ascending=False)

# Get the top 20 jurisdictions
top_20= jurisdiction_deaths_sorted.head(20)


bar_fig = px.bar(
    top_20,
    x="All_Cause",
    y="Jurisdiction_of_Occurrence",
    title="Top 20 Jurisdictions Ranked by Total All-Cause Deaths",
    color="All_Cause",
    color_continuous_scale="Blues",
    labels={"All_Cause":"All Cause",
            "Jurisdiction_of_Occurrence": "Jurisdiction of Occurrence"}
).update_layout(coloraxis_showscale=False)

bar_fig
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: true

import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px

# Ensure date column is properly formatted
wkds_2023['Week_Ending_Date'] = pd.to_datetime(wkds_2023['Week_Ending_Date'], errors='coerce')

# Define target jurisdictions
selected_jurisdictions = [
    "California", "Florida", "Texas",
    "Massachusetts", "Wisconsin", "South Carolina"
]

# Filter the dataset
filtered_df = wkds_2023[wkds_2023['Jurisdiction_of_Occurrence'].isin(selected_jurisdictions)]

# Create line chart
fig = px.line(
    filtered_df,
    x='Week_Ending_Date',
    y='All_Cause',
    color='Jurisdiction_of_Occurrence',
    title='All-Cause Deaths Over Time (Selected Jurisdictions)',
    labels={
        'All_Cause': 'All-Cause Deaths',
        'Week_Ending_Date': 'Week Ending Date',
        'Jurisdiction_of_Occurrence': 'Jurisdiction'
    },
    markers=True
)

# Update layout for styling
fig.update_layout(
    legend=dict(
        orientation='h',
        x=0.5,
        y=-0.2,
        xanchor='center',
        yanchor='top',
        title=dict(text='Jurisdiction', font=dict(size=10)),
        font=dict(family='Arial', size=10, color='black'),
        bgcolor='rgba(0,0,0,0)',  # transparent
    ),
)
```

# REGIONAL

```{python}
# Create regional summary
reg_sum = (
    wkds_2023.groupby("Region")
    .apply(
        lambda g: pd.Series(
            {
                "Average Number of All-Cause Deaths": g["All_Cause"].mean(),
                "Lowest Number of All-Cause Deaths": g["All_Cause"].min(),
                "State with Lowest Deaths": g.loc[g["All_Cause"].idxmin(), "Jurisdiction_of_Occurrence"],
                "Highest All-Cause Deaths": g["All_Cause"].max(),
                "State with Highest All Cause Deaths": g.loc[
                    g["All_Cause"].idxmax(), "Jurisdiction_of_Occurrence"
                ],
            }
        )
    )
    .round(2)
)

itables.show(reg_sum)
```


```{python}
# Summarize diabetes mortality by region
reg_sum_diab2 = (
    wkds_2023.groupby("Region")
    .apply(
        lambda g: pd.Series({
            "Average Diabetes Deaths": g["Diabetes_mellitus__E10_E14_"].mean(),
            "Lowest Diabetes Deaths": g["Diabetes_mellitus__E10_E14_"].min(),
            "State with Lowest Deaths": g.loc[
                g["Diabetes_mellitus__E10_E14_"].idxmin(), "Jurisdiction_of_Occurrence"
            ],
            "Highest Diabetes Deaths": g["Diabetes_mellitus__E10_E14_"].max(),
            "State with Highest Deaths": g.loc[
                g["Diabetes_mellitus__E10_E14_"].idxmax(), "Jurisdiction_of_Occurrence"
            ],
        })
    )
    .round(2)
)

itables.show(reg_sum_diab2)
```

# ABOUT

This interactive dashboard provides a visual exploration of weekly provisional death counts from 2020 to 2023, sourced from the National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS). It allows you to analyze mortality trends across the United States and Puerto Rico, focusing on select underlying causes of death, including COVID-19 (ICD-10 code U07.1).

**Key Features:**

Time Series Analysis: Track weekly death counts over time, identifying trends and potential spikes.

Geographic Comparison: Compare mortality rates and counts across different U.S. states and Puerto Rico.

Cause-Specific Insights: Examine mortality patterns for various underlying causes of death.

COVID-19 Data: Visualize the impact of COVID-19 on weekly death counts.


**Important Notes:**

Data Lag: Please be aware that death counts are presented with a one-week lag.
Data Updates: This dataset will no longer be updated after September 27, 2023. For continued access to similar data, please visit wonder.cdc.gov.

Data Quality: Refer to the data dictionary for detailed information on data quality and limitations.

**Data Source and Citation:**

Source: National Center for Health Statistics.
Suggested Citation: National Center for Health Statistics. Weekly Provisional Counts of Deaths by State and Select Causes, 2020-2023. Date accessed [Last accessed date]. Available from https://data.cdc.gov/d/muzy-jte6.

**Geographic Coverage:**

United States, Puerto Rico.

**Data Dictionary:**

For detailed information on the data fields, please refer to the Data Dictionary. ![] (https://data.cdc.gov/NCHS/Weekly-Provisional-Counts-of-Deaths-by-State-and-S/muzy-jte6/about_data)
This dashboard is designed to provide valuable insights into mortality trends during a critical period. We encourage you to explore the data and utilize the interactive features to gain a deeper understanding of the information.
